```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

This vignette follows CAPTAIN's `univdemo` script. The series is the monthly
airline-passenger record shipped as `datasets::AirPassengers`, which is the
same 144-value `air.dat` series used by the toolbox. Calls keep CAPTAIN's
function names, argument order, and output names. MATLAB's multiple assignment
is a list in R, and `NULL` stands in for `[]`.

`fcast()` uses inclusive sample numbers: `[84 94]` removes samples 84 through
94, and `[131 144]` removes samples 131 through 144. The forecasting line in
the original script is drawn at sample 130, the last sample that remains
observed.

```{r data}
library(captaintvp)

air <- as.numeric(AirPassengers)
TVP <- 1
nvr0 <- 1e-4
y <- fcast(air, rbind(c(84, 94), c(131, 144)))
```

```{r masked-series, fig.cap="Observed airline series and the series with interpolation and forecast samples removed."}
plot(air, type = "l", col = "grey40", xlab = "Sample", ylab = "Passengers")
lines(y, col = "firebrick")
legend("topleft", c("air", "y"), col = c("grey40", "firebrick"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

The first fit is an integrated random walk with the demonstration's initial
noise-variance ratio. `TVP = 1` is CAPTAIN's code for integration order 2.

```{r initial-trend}
initial <- univ(y, numeric(), TVP, nvr0)
fit <- initial$fit
fitse <- initial$fitse
trend <- initial$trend
```

```{r initial-components, fig.cap="Masked observations, initial integrated-random-walk trend, and detrended residual."}
residual <- y - trend
plot(y, type = "l", col = "grey40", xlab = "Sample", ylab = "")
lines(trend, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
lines(residual, col = "darkorange")
legend(
  "topleft",
  c("y", "trend", "y - trend"),
  col = c("grey40", "steelblue", "darkorange"),
  lty = 1, bty = "n"
)
```

`aic()` searches orders 1 through 20 by the Gaussian criterion
`n log(RSS / n) + 2p`, using one estimation sample for every order. CAPTAIN's
published transcript selects order 14. On this implementation the minimum is
higher, but the criterion falls sharply once the seasonal lags enter and order
14 remains competitive with the minimum.

```{r aic}
poly <- aic(y - trend, 20)
p <- length(poly) - 1
aic_table <- attr(poly, "aic")
p
```

```{r aic-path, fig.cap="AIC for the detrended perturbation. The dashed line is the minimizing order."}
plot(aic_table$order, aic_table$aic, type = "b", xlab = "AR order", ylab = "AIC")
abline(v = p, lty = 2)
```

The script then estimates the selected perturbation polynomial and rescales the
trend NVR. The rescaling multiplies `nvr0` by the ratio of the initial
concentrated disturbance variance to the AR innovation variance.

```{r selected-model}
estimated <- univopt(y, seq_len(p), TVP, nvr0, out = 0)
nvr <- estimated$nvr
ARp <- estimated$ARp
nvr
```

For comparison with the CAPTAIN 9.0.6 transcript, the same estimator is also
run at the published order 14. The signs of the large coefficients agree. The
remaining differences come from the Kalman initialization and least-squares
treatment of the internal gap; CAPTAIN's smoother is not available as source.

```{r published-order}
published_arp <- c(
  -0.6076, -0.1137, -0.0526, 0.1670, -0.1447,
  0.2348, -0.1281, 0.1891, -0.1225, 0.2281,
  -0.1813, -0.8041, 0.4586, 0.3524
)
published_nvr <- 2.5934e-3
order14 <- univopt(y, 1:14, TVP, nvr0, out = 0)
comparison <- data.frame(
  lag = seq_along(published_arp),
  captaintvp = round(order14$ARp, 4),
  CAPTAIN = published_arp,
  difference = round(order14$ARp - published_arp, 4)
)
comparison
c(captaintvp = order14$nvr, CAPTAIN = published_nvr)
```

The figures below use the published order so that they correspond to the
transcript. With an AR perturbation and no extra observation noise, the fitted
signal passes through the samples supplied to `univ()`. Uncertainty appears in
the trend and seasonal split and, more visibly, across the missing samples.

```{r final-fit}
final <- univ(y, order14$ARp, TVP, order14$nvr)
fit <- final$fit
fitse <- final$fitse
trend <- final$trend
trendse <- final$trendse
comp <- final$comp
y0 <- final$y0
```

```{r data-and-trend, fig.cap="Airline series and the jointly smoothed trend."}
plot(trend, type = "l", col = "steelblue", lwd = 2, xlab = "Sample", ylab = "Passengers")
lines(air, col = "grey40")
legend("topleft", c("trend", "air"), col = c("steelblue", "grey40"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

```{r seasonal-component, fig.cap="Autoregressive perturbation about the trend."}
plot(comp, type = "l", col = "darkgreen", xlab = "Sample", ylab = "Component")
title("Total seasonal component")
```

```{r fit-and-residuals, fig.cap="Fit, original data, and residuals, with the interpolation interval and forecast origin marked."}
residual <- fit - air
plot(fit, type = "l", col = "steelblue", xlab = "Sample", ylab = "", ylim = range(c(residual, air, fit)))
lines(air, col = "firebrick")
lines(residual, col = "grey40")
abline(v = c(84, 94, 130), col = "firebrick", lty = 2)
legend(
  "topleft",
  c("fit", "air", "fit - air"),
  col = c("steelblue", "firebrick", "grey40"),
  lty = 1, bty = "n"
)
title("Data, fit and residuals")
```

```{r forecast-band, fig.cap="Final two years with the smoothed fit and a two-standard-error band."}
index <- seq_along(fit)
window <- index >= 119
plot(index[window], fit[window], type = "l", col = "steelblue",
  xlab = "Sample", ylab = "Passengers", ylim = c(250, 700))
points(index[window], air[window], col = "firebrick")
lines(index[window], fit[window] + 2 * fitse[window], lty = 2, col = "steelblue")
lines(index[window], fit[window] - 2 * fitse[window], lty = 2, col = "steelblue")
abline(v = 130, col = "firebrick", lty = 2)
legend("topleft", c("fit", "fit ± 2 fitse", "air"),
  col = c("steelblue", "steelblue", "firebrick"),
  lty = c(1, 2, NA), pch = c(NA, NA, 1), bty = "n")
title("Data (o), fit and standard errors")
```

The band is narrow while observations are supplied and opens after sample 130.
The interpolated values returned in `y0` use the fit only at the samples
`fcast()` removed.

```{r interpolation-check}
missing <- which(is.na(y))
all.equal(y0[missing], fit[missing])
all.equal(y0[-missing], y[-missing])
```
